mainTopic: Women and time-bound positive מצוות: how firm the rule is, and where it comes from
overview: The ברייתא finishes its examples of time-bound positive מצוות with תפילין, then lists מצוות that apply at all times, such as מזוזה and מעקה. The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule. Women must keep some time-bound מצוות, like מצה, שמחה and הקהל, and they are exempt from some that are not time-bound, like תלמוד תורה. רבי יוחנן answers that general rules in a משנה are not exception-free, even when they say 'חוץ', and the גמרא proves this from the עירוב list. Next the גמרא gives the source of the exemption. All time-bound מצוות are learned from תפילין, and תפילין is learned from תלמוד תורה, since the two are written side by side twice in שמע. Women are still obligated in מזוזה, because its reward of long life applies to them too. The גמרא then asks why סוכה needed the word האזרח to exempt women. אביי explains that without it we might have thought a סוכה is like a home shared by husband and wife. רבא begins a different answer, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Examples of time-bound and non-time-bound positive מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends its list of time-bound מצוות עשה with תפילין, then lists non-time-bound ones: מזוזה, מעקה, אבידה, and שילוח הקן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And תפילין is also a time-bound positive מצוה. And what is a positive מצוה that is not time-bound? מזוזה, a fence on the roof, returning a lost item, and sending away the mother bird from the nest.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its examples of time-bound positive מצוות and then gives examples of positive מצוות that apply at all times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says women are exempt from מצוות עשה שהזמן גרמא, positive מצוות tied to a time. The ברייתא shows what fits each group: תפילין are tied to a time, but מזוזה, מעקה, אבידה, and שילוח הקן apply anytime, so women are obligated in them.

keyTerms.meaning: A positive מצוה caused by (tied to) a specific time
תפילין, a time-bound מצוה
The מזוזה on the doorpost
A protective fence around a roof
Sending away the mother bird before taking the young or eggs

phrases.english: And tefillin.
And what is a positive מצוה
that is not caused by time?
Mezuzah, a roof fence,
a lost item, and sending away the mother bird from the nest.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵיזוֹהִי מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁלֹּא הַזְּמַן גְּרָמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's examples that define the categories in the משנה's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תפילין are time-bound; מזוזה, מעקה, אבידה, and שילוח הקן are not time-bound.

steps.title: Time-bound מצוות that women must still do
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether this is really a fixed rule, since מצה, שמחה, and הקהל are time-bound and women are still obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this really a rule? Look at מצה, rejoicing on the festival, and the הקהל gathering. They are time-bound positive מצוות, and yet women are obligated!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule by pointing to time-bound מצוות that women must keep anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule says women are exempt from time-bound positive מצוות. Here are three time-bound מצוות where women are obligated. So the rule seems to have exceptions in one direction.

keyTerms.meaning: A general rule
Eating מצה on the first night of פסח
The מצוה to rejoice on a festival
The gathering of all the people to hear the תורה read, held at a set time

phrases.english: But is it a general rule?
There are matzah, rejoicing, and the assembly,
which are positive מצוות caused by time,
and women are obligated!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the general rule that the examples just illustrated.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that women are exempt from time-bound positive מצוות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counterexamples: time-bound מצוות where women are nonetheless obligated.

steps.title: Non-time-bound מצוות that women do not have to do
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a second problem: תלמוד תורה, פריה ורביה, and פדיון הבן are not time-bound, yet women are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And more: look at studying תורה, having children, and redeeming the firstborn son. They are not time-bound positive מצוות, and yet women are exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second challenge from the other direction: מצוות that are not time-bound, yet women are exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule suggests women are obligated in positive מצוות that are not time-bound. These three מצוות are not tied to a time, but women are still exempt. So the rule fails in both directions.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore; adding another point
The מצוה to study תורה
The מצוה to have children
Redeeming a firstborn son from a כהן

phrases.english: And furthermore:
There is Torah study,
having children, and redeeming the firstborn son,
which are not positive מצוות
caused by time,
and women are exempt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the previous challenge with counterexamples from the opposite direction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication that women are obligated in positive מצוות that are not time-bound.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counterexamples: non-time-bound מצוות where women are nonetheless exempt.

steps.title: General rules are not meant to be exception-free
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that we do not learn from general rules, even when the rule lists an exception with 'חוץ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: We do not learn practical הלכה from general rules, even in a place where it says 'except'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers both challenges by saying a general rule in the משנה is not meant to cover every single case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenges assumed the משנה's rule must hold with no exceptions. רבי יוחנן says general statements are not meant that way, so exceptions like מצה or תלמוד תורה do not disprove the rule. He adds that this is true even where the rule itself names an exception with 'חוץ', which would seem to mean that nothing else is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not learn practical הלכה from general rules
Except; a word that excludes a specific case from a rule

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying the rule is wrong. He is saying it is a general guideline that still has exceptions.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle applies across all of ש״ס: a general rule in a משנה does not prove that every case is included.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
We do not learn from general rules,
and even in a place
where it says 'except',

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵין לְמֵדִין מִן הַכְּלָלוֹת
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the nature of the rule: it is general, not exception-free.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's rule was assumed to cover every positive מצוה without exception.
steps.terutzMaskana: General rules in the משנה allow exceptions, even when an explicit 'חוץ' is stated.

steps.title: Proof from a list about עירובין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה from עירובין to support רבי יוחנן's rule: it says you can use any food for an עירוב except water and salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: You can make an עירוב or a שיתוף with any food, except water and salt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is bringing a proof for רבי יוחנן's rule. It quotes a משנה that sounds like a complete list with an 'except'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה looks like a closed rule: everything works, and only water and salt are left out. The next line will show that the list is actually missing items, which proves רבי יוחנן's point.

keyTerms.meaning: Making an עירוב (joining courtyards or שבת boundaries)
Making a שיתוף מבואות (joining an alleyway for carrying on שבת)
Except

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה:
With everything one may make an עירוב and a שיתוף,
except for water and salt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support רבי יוחנן's principle from step 4.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that general rules are not reliable, even when they say 'except'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in עירובין: בכל מערבין ומשתתפין חוץ מן המים ומלח.

steps.title: The list is missing truffles and mushrooms
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the עירוב list is incomplete: truffles and mushrooms also cannot be used, even though the משנה did not mention them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there nothing else? But there are truffles and mushrooms, which also cannot be used!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a hole in the משנה's list. This is part of the proof, setting up the conclusion in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the 'except' list were complete, truffles and mushrooms should be allowed. But they are not allowed, so the list must have left things out. That shows that even a list with 'except' is not a complete rule.

keyTerms.meaning: And is there nothing else?
Truffles
Mushrooms

phrases.english: And is there nothing else?
But there are truffles and mushrooms!
phrases.notes: These also can't be used for an עירוב, even though the משנה didn't list them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the gap in the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of the list in the משנה of עירובין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Truffles and mushrooms are also not allowed for an עירוב, yet the משנה left them off the 'except' list.

steps.title: So general rules are not complete
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that we do not learn from general rules, even when they include an 'except'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we see that we do not learn from general rules, even when the rule says 'except'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof by repeating רבי יוחנן's rule, now backed up by the עירוב example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same principle answers the questions from steps 2 and 3. The משנה's general rule, that women are exempt from time-bound positive מצוות and obligated in the others, was never meant to have no exceptions. So מצה, שמחה and הקהל (where women are obligated) and תלמוד תורה, פריה ורביה and פדיון הבן (where women are exempt) do not disprove it.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not learn from general rules
General rules

steps.whatToRemember: A rule stated in general terms, even one with a list of exceptions, may still have other exceptions that were not mentioned.

phrases.english: Rather, we do not learn from general rules,
even in a place where it says 'except.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the proof in steps 5-6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: General rules, even with listed exceptions, are not complete; this explains the exceptions raised in steps 2-3.

steps.title: Where do we learn the exemption for time-bound מצוות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that women are exempt from positive מצוות that depend on time.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that women are exempt from time-bound positive מצוות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: it asks for the Torah source of the basic rule. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא discussed how far the rule goes. Now it asks where the rule itself comes from in the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: A positive מצוה that depends on time
From where do we know?
Exempt (said of women)

phrases.english: And a positive מצוה that depends on time,
that women are exempt, from where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the scope of the rule to its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that women are exempt from מצוות עשה שהזמן גרמא.

steps.title: Learned from תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The rule is learned from תפילין: just as women are exempt from תפילין, they are exempt from all time-bound positive מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn it from תפילין. Just as women are exempt from תפילין, so too they are exempt from every time-bound positive מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that תפילין is the model case, and every other time-bound מצוה follows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תפילין is a time-bound מצוה, since it is not worn at night or on שבת, and women are exempt from it. The גמרא uses it as the example for all similar מצוות. This raises the obvious question of how we know women are exempt from תפילין itself.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns it from (one case to another)
Just as... so too (a comparison)

phrases.english: He learns it from תפילין:
just as women are exempt from תפילין,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כׇּל מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁהַזְּמַן גְּרָמָא
phrases.english: so too every positive מצוה that depends on time,
women are exempt.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule is learned from תפילין, a time-bound מצוה from which women are exempt.

steps.title: תפילין is learned from תלמוד תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know women are exempt from תפילין, and answers that it is learned from תלמוד תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know about תפילין? We learn it from תלמוד תורה: just as women are exempt from תלמוד תורה, so too they are exempt from תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes one level deeper and gives the source for תפילין itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the Torah, the מצוה of teaching Torah and the מצוה of תפילין are written side by side, so the גמרא compares them. Since women are exempt from the מצוה of תלמוד תורה, they are also exempt from תפילין.

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה of studying and teaching Torah
He learns it

steps.confusionAlert: This is a chain: time-bound מצוות are learned from תפילין, and תפילין is learned from תלמוד תורה. Keep the two links separate.

phrases.english: And תפילין itself?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking how we know women are exempt from תפילין in the first place.

phrases.english: He learns it from תלמוד תורה:
just as women are exempt from תלמוד תורה,
so too women are exempt from תפילין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the base case used in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תפילין is compared to תלמוד תורה, from which women are exempt.

steps.title: Why not compare תפילין to מזוזה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: תפילין is also written next to מזוזה, so why not compare it to מזוזה, where women are obligated?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us compare תפילין to מזוזה instead!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the comparison it just made. It suggests a different comparison that would lead to the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מזוזה is written right after תפילין in the Torah, and women are obligated in מזוזה. If we compared תפילין to מזוזה, women would be obligated in תפילין, and then the source for the whole rule would fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: And let us compare them, because they are written next to each other
The scroll placed on the doorpost

phrases.english: But let us compare תפילין to מזוזה!
phrases.notes: Women are obligated in מזוזה, so this comparison would make them obligated in תפילין too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison made in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice to compare תפילין to תלמוד תורה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תפילין is also written next to מזוזה, which would make women obligated.

steps.title: The link to תלמוד תורה is stronger
steps.stepSummary: תפילין is placed next to תלמוד תורה in both paragraphs of שמע, but next to מזוזה only in the first, so the תלמוד תורה comparison wins.
steps.simpleTranslation: תפילין is placed next to תלמוד תורה in both the first and the second paragraph, but in the second paragraph it is not placed next to מזוזה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by comparing how often each pair appears together in the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first paragraph of שמע, תפילין sits between תלמוד תורה and מזוזה. In the second paragraph, ולמדתם (תלמוד תורה) comes between תפילין and מזוזה. So תפילין is connected to תלמוד תורה twice and to מזוזה only once, which makes the link to תלמוד תורה stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: They were compared (placed side by side in the Torah)
The first paragraph of שמע
The second paragraph of שמע (והיה אם שמוע)

phrases.english: תפילין was compared to תלמוד תורה
both in the first paragraph
and in the second paragraph,
but תפילין to מזוזה, in the second paragraph,
phrases.notes: In the second paragraph, the verse about learning Torah sits between תפילין and מזוזה.

phrases.english: they were not compared.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: תפילין might be compared to מזוזה, which would obligate women.
steps.terutzMaskana: תפילין is linked to תלמוד תורה twice and to מזוזה only once, so women are exempt from תפילין.

steps.title: Then compare מזוזה to תלמוד תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if they are written next to each other, let us compare מזוזה to תלמוד תורה and exempt women from מזוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then let us compare מזוזה to תלמוד תורה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge from the other direction: perhaps women should be exempt from מזוזה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second paragraph of שמע, מזוזה is written right after ולמדתם, the תלמוד תורה verse. If that placement counts, women should be exempt from מזוזה just as they are from תלמוד תורה.

phrases.english: But let us compare מזוזה to תלמוד תורה!
phrases.notes: That would make women exempt from מזוזה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same side-by-side logic from step 12 against women's obligation in מזוזה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מזוזה sits next to תלמוד תורה in the second paragraph, so it should share the exemption.

steps.title: מזוזה promises life, which women need too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison: the Torah promises long life for מזוזה, and women need life just as men do.
steps.simpleTranslation: That can't be! It is written, 'So that your days may be many.' Do men need life and women not need life?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea of exempting women from מזוזה, using the reward the Torah gives for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right after מזוזה, the פסוק promises long life. A reward of life clearly applies to women as well. So this פסוק outweighs the side-by-side comparison, and women stay obligated in מזוזה.

keyTerms.meaning: That can't even enter your mind
So that your days may be many
Men... women

steps.whatToRemember: Women are exempt from תפילין because it is linked to תלמוד תורה, and that is the source for all מצוות עשה שהזמן גרמא. Women are still obligated in מזוזה, because its reward of long life applies to everyone.

phrases.english: It can't enter your mind,
as it is written: 'So that your days may be many,'
do men need life,
and women do not need life?!

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proposed comparison of מזוזה to תלמוד תורה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק promises long life for מזוזה, and that reward clearly applies to women too.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why women are obligated in מזוזה even though they are exempt from תפילין.

steps.title: Why does סוכה need a special word to exempt women?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that סוכה is a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, yet the תורה needed a special word, האזרח, to exempt women. That suggests that without it women would be obligated, which goes against the general rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at סוכה. It is a positive מצוה tied to a set time, since it says 'In סוכות you shall live for seven days.' Even so, women are exempt only because the תורה wrote 'the homeborn' to leave them out. That means that otherwise women would be obligated!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the general rule that women are exempt from every time-bound positive מצוה. It uses סוכה as a counter-example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If women were automatically exempt from every מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, the תורה would not need the word האזרח to exempt them from סוכה. Since the תורה did write it, it seems that without it women would be obligated. So the general rule looks shaky.

keyTerms.meaning: A positive מצוה that only applies at a certain time
The hut we live in during the seven days of סוכות
'The Merciful One', a name for ה׳ as the One who gave the תורה
'The homeborn', the word in the פסוק used to leave women out
'But if it were not so', meaning without this, the opposite would be true

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not questioning whether women are exempt from סוכה. Everyone agrees they are. The question is why a special word was needed if there is already a general rule.

phrases.english: But there is סוכה,
which is a positive מצוה that depends on time,
as it is written: 'In סוכות you shall live for seven days,'
and the reason is that the Merciful One wrote 'the homeborn'
phrases.notes: The extra ה at the start, meaning 'the', is read as narrowing who is included.

phrases.english: to leave out the women,
so if not for that, women would be obligated!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי סוּכָּה דְּמִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁהַזְּמַן גְּרָמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the תפילין and מזוזה comparisons, the גמרא now tests the general exemption rule against סוכה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The general rule that women are exempt from every מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A special exclusion word for סוכה implies that without it women would be obligated. That suggests there is no general automatic exemption.

steps.title: אביי: סוכה is like a home, so a special word was needed
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the word האזרח was needed for סוכה. Otherwise we might have thought that, since living in a סוכה is like living in a home, husband and wife must live there together.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The word was needed. You might have thought this: since it says 'In סוכות you shall live,' that means live there the way you live at home. Just as a home is for a man and his wife together, a סוכה is also for a man and his wife together.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge. He shows that סוכה had a special reason to think women might be obligated, so the general rule still stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule would normally exempt women. But the word תשבו compares the סוכה to a home, and a home is shared by husband and wife. That comparison could have overridden the general rule, so the תורה wrote האזרח to confirm that women are still exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was needed', used when explaining why a word or teaching is not extra
'It would have entered your mind to say', introducing a mistaken first thought
'Sit' in the סוכה the way you live in your home
A home, a place where one lives

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer keeps the general rule that women are exempt from time-bound positive מצוות. It explains that סוכה needed its own word only because of its comparison to a home.

phrases.english: אביי said: It was needed,
because you might have thought to say:
since it is written 'In סוכות you shall live,'
'you shall live' means the way you live at home:
just as a home is for a man and his wife,
so too a סוכה is for a man and his wife.
